Hi Alice - great to meet earlier today. Thanks for walking us through FinCoBank's requirements. Below is a short recap from our side and the action items we committed to.

Recap of needs you mentioned:
- Primary ask: exportable audit logs that show who accessed what data and when (user identity, resource, action, timestamp, request metadata).
- Field-level awareness for PII: flagging/redaction options for fields like SSN, DOB, account numbers.
- Export formats: CSV or JSONL preferred for your security tooling.
- Retention: you mentioned 7 years for regulatory purposes; please confirm if that applies to all logs or a subset.
- Data residency: FinCoBank requires logs stored in US-only regions for this project.

Action items (from Redwood):
1) I will send a sample audit log export (CSV) and a short doc describing the fields and schema by EOD tomorrow.
2) We will confirm our retention/archival options and how to scope retention by project/environment.
3) Engineering to confirm PII redaction/pseudonymization options and whether access-level metadata is preserved after redaction.
4) Schedule a technical follow-up / demo with your security engineering team - suggested times in the links below.

Are there any additional log fields you need (e.g., client IP, API key id, request id)? If you can share your security questionnaire, I can route to our compliance team.

Thanks - will follow up with the sample export.

Thanks Marissa - that recap looks right. A few clarifications from our side:

- Required fields in audit export: timestamp (ISO8601), actor (user id + role), action (read/write/export), resource id (record id), field list accessed (if possible), request id, client IP, and service node id.
- PII handling: we require the raw access metadata to indicate that PII was accessed (e.g., field-level marker) even if the PII values themselves are redacted in exported datasets.
- Retention: yes, 7 years for access logs related to regulated accounts. Non-regulated accounts can be 2 years.
- Residency: logs must be stored in the US for this engagement.
- Export: provide CSV with a header row and a JSONL option; both are fine.

Attached is our security questionnaire and a short checklist. Could you confirm whether your platform provides an automated export endpoint (S3/HTTPS) and whether exports include full request metadata? Also, we will need a screenshot or evidence of the access control UI or an example of an audit query demonstrating "who accessed X record on Y date".

Requesting procurement to add this to the SOW and share timelines.

Appreciate the quick turnaround - Alice

--
Alice Morgan
Security Engineering Manager | FinCoBank

Hi Alice - thanks for the clear list. Please find attached a sanitized sample export and a screenshot of the access-log UI. Notes below:

What we attached:
- audit_logs_export_sample.csv (CSV, header row included). The sample includes: timestamp (ISO8601), actor_id, actor_role, action, resource_id, fields_accessed (comma-separated), request_id, client_ip, service_node_id. PII values are redacted; fields_accessed lists which PII fields were touched.
- SOC2-Screenshot-Access-Logs.png (screenshot of UI showing per-record access history and filter by user/date).
- security-questionnaire.pdf (copied from your earlier email for reference).

Notes on exports and retention:
- Export endpoints: we support scheduled exports to S3 and on-demand exports via the Console or API (JSONL or CSV). We can push daily or on-demand snapshots to a customer-owned S3 bucket over HTTPS with server-side encryption.
- Retention: retention is configurable per customer/tenant. We can set retention to 7 years for regulated accounts and shorter for others; archived logs can be exported to your S3 for long-term storage (immutable archives supported via customer-managed lifecycle rules).
- PII handling: redaction/pseudonymization of PII is supported in export output while preserving a fields_accessed marker in the audit row. Original raw logs (for internal forensic use) are retained according to the retention policy and are subject to customer access controls.
- Evidence: for your audit we can provide a console screenshot and a short recorded demo; for attestation we can supply export metadata and a configuration snapshot showing retention settings. For SOC2 artifacts, we can share redacted evidence under an NDA if needed.

Next steps:
1) Confirm which export cadence and format you prefer (daily S3 push vs on-demand).
2) If you want the recorded demo, please pick a time here: https://calendar.google.com/event?eid=demo-20260904
3) Procurement - let me know if you need any extra items for the SOW (attestation language, sample SLA).

If you need additional fields in the CSV please let me know and we can re-run the sample.

Best,
